structural_reasons: STRUCTURAL GAP (narrowed): this plan is PARTIALLY participant-directed per its own Form 5500 codes (2H, no 2G/404(c) code filed). A trustee-directed sleeve could hold this wrapper directly (cell 3.5), and the daily-menu constraint applies only to the participant-directed portion, where the menu assumes daily liquidity whereas this wrapper deals quarterly with a 5% cap per quarter on outstanding shares.

Facts missing for a structural verdict: gating history (per-offer tendered-vs-purchased counts not printed in on-disk filings. Sept 2025 offer was Board-UPSIZED (demand signal). Proration incidence unevidenced). The verdict stays partial until they are read from the filings.
Early repurchase economics: not on record (2.7). Relevant to participant-level churn (2.7).
scenario_reasons: Capacity: 5% per quarter on outstanding shares: at most 20% of the position per year. This is a FUND-level cap shared by every holder, so the plan's position is served only while offers are not oversubscribed.

Filed outflow proxy (Schedule H, plan year 2024-01-01 to 2024-12-31): 6.5% of the position per year vs 20% annual wrapper capacity, the plan's total expenses less administrative expenses over beginning net assets, applied to the position. Adequate headroom at the filed rate if offers are not prorated.

Slider assumption (illustrative): 13.7% of the position per year vs 20% annual wrapper capacity, from tail turnover 20%/yr on the 58.2% of accounts that are separated and active turnover 5%/yr on the rest. Shown beside the filed rate, not blended with it. THIN HEADROOM: the slider assumption consumes over 60% of wrapper capacity, so proration in any oversubscribed window would push the shortfall into the next window.

Fund capacity in dollars: 20% of approx. $5.8B net assets (cell 3.6) is $1.2B per year. At a 5% allocation ($490.5M) the plan's demand at the filed rate is $31.9M per year, 2.73% of that capacity. The cap is shared by every holder, so this is the plan's own claim on it, not the fund's total demand. The allocation moves these dollar figures and this share, never the percent-of-position ladder.

Scenario verdict (ILLUSTRATIVE, this plan): conditional. No rung fired: the filed outflow proxy 6.5% and the stressed demand 19.2% of the position per year both stay within the annual wrapper capacity 20% (binding cap 5% per quarter on outstanding shares (3.1), quarterly offers (3.1), program active as of 2026-03-31 (3.1), gating history not on record (3.3)). Per quarter: filed 1.6% and stressed 4.8% of the position against the 5% cap. Proration assumption: an oversubscribed offer is filled pro rata and the unfilled remainder waits for the next window.

Schedule H benefit-payment line 2e is not yet in the plan record. The filed outflow proxy (total expenses less administrative expenses over beginning net assets) stands in for it as the base demand, and the turnover assumptions are the stress around it.

filed_outflow.label: filed outflow proxy
filed_outflow.formula: (total expenses minus total administrative expenses) / net assets at the beginning of the plan year * 100
filed_outflow.source: Schedule H totals of the plan's Form 5500 for plan year 2024-01-01 to 2024-12-31, from the plan record
filed_outflow.what: total expenses less administrative expenses over beginning net assets, an upper bound on benefit payments while Schedule H line 2e is not in the record

stressed_scenario.assumptions: the filed outflow proxy plus the increment the stress multiples add under stress (tail turnover x2, active turnover x1.5 over the slider assumption)
stressed_scenario.outcome: within wrapper capacity (19.2% vs 20%) IF offers are not prorated

fund_capacity.basis: plan demand = allocation share * plan net assets * filed outflow proxy, fund capacity = binding annual cap * fund net assets
